text:
sylvia: heads up — saw a transient cluster-wide spike in write amplification on a us-west3 nvme cohort at ~08:02 UTC, coinciding with GPU attach failures for batch jobs. attach rate dropped ~30% for ~3m and some pods landed on fallback nodes.

dan: logs? which cohort / pool?

sylvia: cohort gn-west3-3 (ephemeral pool). iostat/blk reports show tinywrite ratio spike and high fsync stalls. pasted sample: ```iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1        2.00  380.00    12.00 10240.00   54.00    5.12 12.3   0.3    12.0   5.1   99.9
```

kai: that util line is scary — looks like fsync coalescing isn't working and janitor/cleaner runs are overlapping with batch windows. any scrub logs?

sylvia: cleaner shows back-to-back scrubs 08:01:45 -> 08:03:10 on multiple hosts. eng-cleaner-bot: "started scrub" messages queued then 429s for scheduling.

leo: region note — us-west3 has a lower spare-ssd margin right now (capacity reclaim running). we recently tightened scrub cadence to reduce wear and must have bumped overlap risk.

dan: impact on GPU provisioning? was this blocking launches or just slowdown?

sylvia: mix — some launches timed out and triggered retry/fallback; others succeeded but latency spiked causing autoscaler to mis-evaluate utilization. overall cost increased due to fallback remote nodes coming online.

kai: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle janitor scrubs in us-west3 for 10m, 2) bump ephemeral attach timeout to avoid immediate fallback, 3) temporarily route new batch jobs to eu-west or dedicated pool. which do we prefer?

leo: prefer 1 + 2 short-term. routing is costly and impacts latency. we can enable scrub backoff window tagged by maintenance flag.

sylvia: agreed. I'll patch the cleaner schedule: set min-splay to 300s and add coalesce guard for concurrent scrubs per-pool. planning to roll in 5m. also raising attach timeout from 30s -> 60s.

eng-cleaner-bot: issued command: `cleaner set-backoff --pool gn-west3-3 --duration 600s`

dan: monitor dashboards and gating: watch nvme %util, avgqu-sz, and gpu-attach success rate for next 20m. if attach still fails, we'll failover a small set of nodes to dedicated capacity.

sylvia: will do. adding a short eval query: `sum(rate(nvme_io_time_seconds_total[1m])) by (cohort)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(gpu_attach_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))` — will ping when stable. :eyes:

kai: also file a follow-up to revisit scrub cadence vs wear tradeoff — this pattern could reappear as load increases.

leo: noted. cost impact estimate for fallback nodes this morning ~+$1.2k/hr for the 6min window. we'll include in the incident cost log.

sylvia: update: after applying backoff at 08:05 UTC, attach success normalized by 08:09. leaving the backoff for 20m and then we'll slowly reintroduce scrubs with coalesce guard. closing loop here, will post postmortem if anything recurs. :thumbsup:
